open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_router.create_app`
open_points.text: Every other route has the token and the project id judged by `module:deliverer_api`, calls one operation of `module:photo_delivery`, and answers every refusal through `module:deliverer_api`.
open_points.question: Are the project id and photo-delivery operation reached only after token acceptance, as A5 rule 1 requires, or does this sentence require every request to reach them?
options: Stop immediately when token validation fails; do not inspect the project id, body or delivery operation
Judge the project id and call the delivery operation even when token validation fails
open_points.default_guess: Stop immediately on a token refusal, before inspecting identifiers or the body and without calling `photo_delivery`.

witness.initial: The scan route receives no token and a malformed project id.
outcomes: A5 rule 1 gives an unauthorized refusal before the project id is examined, and `photo_delivery` is not called.
The changed State 5 sentence is read literally: the project id is judged and the scan operation is called as well as producing the token refusal.
witness.observer: The calling flow and any instrumentation of the connections-file read

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_router.create_app`
open_points.text: The surface serves only the four routes.
open_points.question: What must happen for an unknown path, a declared path with the wrong method, a declared path with an added trailing slash, and framework-generated HEAD or OPTIONS requests?
options: Use framework defaults, including any redirect, 404, 405, HEAD or OPTIONS behavior
Return 404 for every request that is not an exact method-and-path pair
Redirect trailing-slash variants but return 404 or 405 for the other cases
open_points.default_guess: Disable generated routes, retain framework 404 and 405 answers, and retain its trailing-slash redirect behavior.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_router.create_app`
open_points.text: A served route answers a wrong token, a malformed request and every M08 refusal.
open_points.question: Which malformed requests are handled as M08 by `refusal_answer`, and which malformed HTTP requests or routing failures retain the framework's own status and body?
options: Convert only token, project-id, request-model and declared service refusals to M08
Convert every error occurring on a declared route, including framework parsing and method errors, to M08
Let framework request-model validation retain its native answer while converting only explicit service refusals
open_points.default_guess: Convert token, project-id, body-model and service refusals to M08; retain framework-native answers for requests that do not reach a declared route.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_service.run_service`
open_points.text: START_FAILED before it listens, SERVED when a signal of the imported `STOP_SIGNALS` constant stops its web server after it has begun listening, and SERVER_FAILED for any other end after that.
open_points.question: What exact event changes the outcome domain from START_FAILED to SERVED or SERVER_FAILED: binding the socket, accepting connections, or the web server's startup-complete report?
options: The socket is successfully bound
The socket can accept connections
The web server emits its startup-complete report
open_points.default_guess: Use the web server's startup-complete report, with its socket accepting connections, as the boundary.

witness.initial: The server binds its socket and then fails during startup before reporting readiness.
events: Startup code fails before the server reports startup complete.
outcomes: If binding means listening, the outcome is SERVER_FAILED.
If startup-complete means listening, the outcome is START_FAILED.
witness.observer: The deployment, through the process exit status

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_service.run_service`
open_points.text: SERVED when a signal of the imported `STOP_SIGNALS` constant stops its web server after it has begun listening, and SERVER_FAILED for any other end after that.
open_points.question: Which outcome applies when a stop signal begins shutdown but shutdown subsequently fails, or when a server failure and signal occur together?
options: Any failure after listening produces SERVER_FAILED, even after a stop signal
The first terminating event wins, so a stop signal produces SERVED despite a later shutdown failure
A received stop signal always produces SERVED unless failure occurred before the signal
open_points.default_guess: Any failure during or after shutdown produces SERVER_FAILED; SERVED requires signal-initiated shutdown to finish without failure.

events: A shutdown hook fails and the process exits unsuccessfully.
outcomes: Classify it as SERVED because SIGTERM stopped the server.
Classify it as SERVER_FAILED because the post-listening end included a failure.
witness.observer: The deployment, through exit status 0 or 1

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.text: A file is read once, and the bytes read are the bytes judged.
open_points.question: Does “read once” mean one complete pass that continues after short reads until EOF or the limit probe, or one invocation of a read operation whose short result is treated as complete?
options: Continue reading after short reads until EOF or one byte beyond the source limit
Perform one read call and judge whatever it returns
Permit either interpretation
open_points.default_guess: Use one open file description and one forward pass, continuing after short reads until EOF or one byte beyond the source limit.

witness.initial: A regular source file is within the source limit, but a read returns a short non-EOF result before later bytes are available from the same opened file.
events: Its first read returns only the initial part.
The implementation decides whether to continue.
outcomes: The full content is hashed and classified.
Only the initial bytes are hashed and classified.
witness.observer: The calling flow, through the reported source id and size

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.text: its EXIF transposition applies the camera orientation
open_points.question: Which exact image-library operation and malformed-or-unusual orientation behavior must implement EXIF transposition?
options: Use the library's dedicated EXIF-transpose operation
Read the orientation tag and manually rotate or mirror
Apply only rotations and ignore mirror orientations or malformed tags
open_points.default_guess: Use the pinned image library's dedicated EXIF-transpose operation on the first frame.

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.text: A camera value is unusable when it does not match the imported `EXIF_DATETIME_PATTERN` constant whole or is no valid calendar date and time, when its UTC year is before the imported `CAMERA_EARLIEST_YEAR` constant, or when it is more than the imported `CAMERA_LATEST_AFTER_MODIFIED_HOURS` constant of hours after the file's modification time.
open_points.question: Is a syntactically valid calendar time unusable when the runtime datetime type cannot represent it or when conversion to UTC overflows or otherwise fails, or does that failure abort preparation?
options: Treat representation or UTC-conversion failure as unusable and try the next date source
Fail the photo as unreadable
Let the runtime exception escape
open_points.default_guess: Treat any representation or UTC-conversion failure as making that camera value unusable, then try the next source.

witness.initial: EXIF contains `9999:12:31 23:30:00` with a negative offset whose UTC conversion exceeds the runtime datetime range; modification time is usable.
outcomes: The EXIF value is unusable and the modification time becomes the photo moment.
Preparation raises or fails instead of falling back.
witness.observer: The calling flow, through a placed photo versus a failed or refused delivery

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.text: At the start it is read once; its last component must not be a link, while the folders above it belong to the installation and are taken as they stand, and the permissions judged are those of the file that is read.
open_points.question: How must `read_token` ensure that the file checked for link status and permissions is the same file whose bytes are read when the path changes during the operation?
options: Open the last component without following links and inspect and read that opened file
Inspect the path and then open it normally
Open normally, then reject only if the opened file reports itself as a link
open_points.default_guess: Open the final component with no-follow semantics, then inspect permissions and read bytes through that same opened file description.

witness.initial: The credential path names a secure regular file.
events: `read_token` checks that the path is not a symbolic link.
Another actor replaces the last component with a symbolic link to a different readable file.
outcomes: A no-follow open rejects the replacement and startup ends.
A check-then-open implementation follows the replacement and starts with the other file's contents.
witness.observer: The deployment and the caller attempting authentication

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.text: Condition 1 is decided from the name and from the path it names, without following a link at any folder or at the file, and the file that is read is the one at the path that was checked; no file of a folder on the path is read (INV-02).
open_points.question: What operation ties every checked directory component and the final checked file to the object later read when names are replaced concurrently?
options: Walk through held directory handles with no-follow opens and read the final opened file
Check every pathname first and reopen the full pathname for reading
Recheck the path after reading and discard the result if it changed
open_points.default_guess: Walk from an opened photo-folder handle, opening each component without following links, and read and inspect the same final opened file.

witness.initial: `photos/a/p.jpg` is a regular file inside the confirmed folder.
events: Syncthing replaces `a` or `p.jpg` before the final pathname is opened for reading.
outcomes: Handle-relative traversal reads the object that was opened and checked, or fails without following the replacement.
A check-then-reopen traversal reads a different object reached by the same textual path.
witness.observer: The calling flow and owner, through the source hash and stored image
